newsitem.title: UK: Copper jogs higher on thin LME pre-market.
newsitem.headline: Copper jogs higher on thin LME pre-market.

text.p: LME copper bounced on Tuesday morning, largely on short-covering, but was expected to come under selling pressure later on in ring trading, traders said.
Three months copper touched a high of $2,274 per tonne in thin conditions, up from Monday's kerb close of $2,257, but light selling came in at the highs, they added.
"It seems to be merely a bounce from the oversold conditions of yesterday," one trader said. "I think we could well see some scale-up selling later on."
On Monday, copper sank to $2,245 but rebounded in the afternoon on bargain-hunting and short-covering.

Resistance was pegged around $2,280/90, with first support at Monday's low and then at $2,220, analysts said. Chartists said a sloping head and shoulders pattern indicated eventual falls as low as $1,980.
Stocks, which fell by 2,125 tonnes, were within expectations, traders added.
Aluminium was less active, edging $5 higher to $1,554.
Charts were also looking sickly for aluminium and the market was soon expected to test the year's low of $1,534, analysts said.
A breach of that level was likely to send the market down to $1,500, they added.
Zinc and nickel held stronger levels seen on Monday after managing impressive rebounds.
Nickel extended the gains on the pre-market to a high of $7,350, but a stocks rise of 1,872 tonnes temporarily dampened the enthusiasm.
Prices dipped, but showed resilience by clawing back to $7,315, up $75 from Monday's afternoon kerb.
Analysts were wary, however, about the upside potential.
"Any subsequent bounce looks limited to $7,400 against a background of persistent rises in LME stocks, whilst key support remains at $7,110," broker Brandeis said in a commentary.
Zinc was steady in a tight range, last at $1,254, up $1.
Resistance was pegged at $1,260/70, with first support at $1,244.
Lead was slightly firmer at $640, up $8, and tin was unchanged at $5,750.
